sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界的一些最具影响力的人物，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: It started with a picture posted on the internet and ended in an extravagant cryptocurrency bidding war.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于互联网上发布的一张图片，并以一场奢华的加密货币竞价战告终。

sentences.en: Now to the latest trend that's sweeping the internet, the skyrocketing prices for digital art sold as NFTs.
sentences.zh: 现在来看席卷互联网的最新趋势，作为 NFT 出售的数字艺术品价格暴涨。

sentences.en: NFT.
sentences.zh: NFT。

sentences.en: NFT.
sentences.zh: NFT。

sentences.en: NFT.
sentences.zh: NFT。

sentences.en: And that stands for non-fungible token.
sentences.zh: 它的全称是不可替代代币。

sentences.en: My colleague, Sabrina
sentences.zh: 我的同事萨布丽娜

sentences.en: Tavernisi, speaks with columnist Kevin Roos about digital currency's newest frontier, his unexpected role in it, and why it actually matters.
sentences.zh: 塔维尼西与专栏作家凯文·罗斯对话，探讨数字货币的最新前沿、他在其中的意外角色，以及它为什么真的很重要。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, April 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月13日，星期二。

sentences.en: So Kevin, I realized how little I understood about your world when I saw this headline of yours in the paper.
sentences.zh: 凯文，当我看到你在报纸上的这个标题时，我意识到我对你的世界了解得太少了。

sentences.en: And I'm going to read it to you right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就读给你听。

sentences.en: So it says, why did someone pay $560,000 for a picture of my column?
sentences.zh: 上面写着：为什么有人花56万美元买了我专栏的一张图片？

sentences.en: So tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这个吧。

sentences.en: Well, actually, that is a little outdated because the exchange rates have fluctuated since I published that column.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实这有点过时了，因为自我发表那篇专栏以来，汇率已经波动了。

sentences.en: So someone actually paid $725,000 for a picture of my column.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上有人花了72.5万美元买了我专栏的一张图片。

sentences.en: So you're saying you sold something that everybody can read online basically for free for hundreds of thousands of real dollars.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，你卖出了一个大家基本上可以在网上免费阅读的东西，价格是几十万美元的真金白银。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I would like to think that all my columns are worth at least $725,000.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我愿意认为我的所有专栏都至少值72.5万美元。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Kevin.
sentences.zh: 凯文。

sentences.en: But that might have been an anomaly.
sentences.zh: 但那可能是一个特例。

sentences.en: But that is the world of NFTs for you.
sentences.zh: 不过这就是 NFT 的世界。

sentences.en: So Kevin, where does the story of NFTs begin?
sentences.zh: 凯文，NFT 的故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: So the story of NFTs really starts with the story of cryptocurrencies, and in particular with
sentences.zh: NFT 的故事其实始于加密货币的故事，尤其是

sentences.en: Bitcoin, which began all the way back in 2008.
sentences.zh: 比特币，它始于遥远的2008年。

sentences.en: During the financial crisis, there was a mortgage meltdown.
sentences.zh: 在金融危机期间，发生了抵押贷款崩盘。

sentences.en: The Federal Reserve was bailing out banks and printing all this money trying to stabilize the economy.
sentences.zh: 美联储一直在救助银行并印制所有这些货币，试图稳定经济。

sentences.en: And in the middle of all this, this mysterious paper appeared on a cryptography email to serve.
sentences.zh: 正是在这一切之中，这篇神秘的论文出现在了一个密码学邮件服务器上。

sentences.en: And it was written by someone calling themselves Satoshi Nakamoto.
sentences.zh: 它是由一个自称中本聪的人撰写的。

sentences.en: And it proposed this new form of digital money called Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 它提出了一种名为比特币的新型数字货币。

sentences.en: And the technology that sort of powered Bitcoin, the infrastructure that allows Bitcoin to work becomes known as the blockchain.
sentences.zh: 支撑比特币的技术、让比特币得以运行的基础设施后来被称为区块链。

sentences.en: So explain both of those to me.
sentences.zh: 向我解释一下这两者。

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You know how money, regular money, is controlled by a central bank.
sentences.zh: 你知道货币，普通货币，是由中央银行控制的。

sentences.en: The Federal Reserve manages the United States dollar.
sentences.zh: 美联储管理着美元。

sentences.en: And the Federal Reserve basically has free reign to do whatever it wants with the dollar.
sentences.zh: 美联储基本上可以随心所欲地处理美元。

sentences.en: It can decide how many dollars there should be, like whether we should print more money or not, based on how much they think the dollar should be worth.
sentences.zh: 它可以根据其认为美元应该值多少钱，来决定应该有多少美元，比如我们是否应该印制更多的钱。

sentences.en: So it's this very centralized system where the government, politicians and institutions, have a lot of control over money, this thing that affects all of us.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个高度集中的系统，政府、政客和机构对货币这种影响我们所有人的东西拥有很大的控制权。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what Satoshi Nakamoto proposed was a totally decentralized system.
sentences.zh: 所以中本聪提出的是一个完全去中心化的系统。

sentences.en: And in this system, there are a finite number of units.
sentences.zh: 在这个系统中，单位数量是有限的。

sentences.en: There will only ever be 21 million Bitcoins.
sentences.zh: 比特币永远只有2100万枚。

sentences.en: And no more can ever be created.
sentences.zh: 再也不能创造更多了。

sentences.en: So everyone knows exactly how many there are, how many there will be.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都知道到底有多少，将来会有多少。

sentences.en: And people can just buy them with regular money and spend them anywhere that accepts Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 人们可以用普通货币购买它们，并在任何接受比特币的地方消费。

sentences.en: Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 比特币。

sentences.en: And instead of the supply and the value of Bitcoins being controlled by a central bank or a government, Bitcoin is controlled by a piece of software called a blockchain.
sentences.zh: 而且，比特币的供应量和价值不是由中央银行或政府控制，而是由一个名为区块链的软件控制。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: And at a very simple level, a blockchain is a network of computers all over the world, thousands of them.
sentences.zh: 在非常简单的层面上，区块链是一个遍布全球的计算机网络，有数千台之多。

sentences.en: And they keep track of every Bitcoin transaction ever made.
sentences.zh: 它们记录着历史上每一笔比特币交易。

sentences.en: So every time a Bitcoin is bought or sold, that transaction gets recorded in this shared global database, kind of like a big Google spreadsheet or something.
sentences.zh: 因此，每当购买或出售比特币时，该交易就会被记录在这个共享的全球数据库中，有点像一个大型的谷歌电子表格什么的。

sentences.en: And anyone with an internet connection can go back and see every change that's ever been made to this database in a very public and transparent and permanent way.
sentences.zh: 任何有互联网连接的人都可以回过头来，以一种公开、透明和永久的方式查看对该数据库所做的每一次更改。

sentences.en: So no one person or institution controls this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以没有任何一个人或机构控制这个东西。

sentences.en: It's just this permissionless distributed computer network that people who are into Bitcoin think is actually more trustworthy than banks that can be manipulated by politicians and governments.
sentences.zh: 它只是这个无需许可的分布式计算机网络，热爱比特币的人认为它实际上比那些会被政客和政府操纵的银行更值得信赖。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So this is ultimately about trust and transparency coming off the distrust people developed after the 2008 financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 所以这归根结底是关于信任和透明度，源于人们在2008年金融危机后产生的不信任感。

sentences.en: And that felt like institutions were manipulating things behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 当时感觉机构在幕后操纵一切。

sentences.en: Whereas here, there's no wizard behind the curtain, no shadowy figures, no politicians, as you say, doing the manipulating.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，幕后没有巫师，没有阴暗的人物，也没有像你说的那些进行操纵的政客。

sentences.en: It's just a bunch of computers that no one controls.
sentences.zh: 它只是一堆没有人控制的计算机。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's essentially taking this giant financial system that is based on human decisions and political considerations and global economies.
sentences.zh: 是的，它本质上是将这个基于人类决策、政治考量和全球经济的庞大金融系统取代。

sentences.en: And it's just replacing it all with computer code.
sentences.zh: 全部用计算机代码取而代之。

sentences.en: Okay, so Kevin, Nakamoto creates this whole new system of buying and selling and tracking those sales.
sentences.zh: 好的，凯文，中本聪创造了一个全新的系统，用于买卖和追踪这些销售。

sentences.en: But so then what happens?
sentences.zh: 但接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: What do people do with it?
sentences.zh: 人们用它做什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so this paper appears on this obscure cryptographic listserv.
sentences.zh: 是的，这篇论文出现在一个鲜为人知的密码学邮件列表中。

sentences.en: And then Satoshi Nakamoto, whoever he or she or they are, disappears.
sentences.zh: 然后中本聪，无论他、她或他们是谁，消失了。

sentences.en: And people sort of take this idea of Bitcoin, and they run with it.
sentences.zh: 人们开始接受比特币这个想法，并将其发扬光大。

sentences.en: Early on, this is sort of an experimental, weird community of people who are really into this new form of money.
sentences.zh: 早期，这是一个实验性的、奇怪的社群，里面的人非常迷恋这种新形式的货币。

sentences.en: And they're just playing around with it.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在玩它。

sentences.en: I mean, they're testing out the technology.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们在测试这项技术。

sentences.en: And Bitcoin at this time is worth basically nothing.
sentences.zh: 当时的比特币基本上没有什么价值。

sentences.en: I mean, each Bitcoin is worth a tiny fraction of a cent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每个比特币只值一美分的一小部分。

sentences.en: So they're doing things like buying pizza.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在做买披萨之类的事情。

sentences.en: When I say Bitcoin, you say what?
sentences.zh: 我说比特币，你说什么？

sentences.en: Pizza.
sentences.zh: 披萨。

sentences.en: There was this programmer in Florida who sort of famously bought two pizzas from Papa John's for 10,000 Bitcoin, which at the time was worth about $25.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州有一位程序员，他做了一件出名的事情：用1万枚比特币从棒约翰那里买了两个披萨，当时这大约值25美元。

sentences.en: I just told people I wanted a pizza and I want to pay with Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 我只是告诉人们我想要一个披萨，我想用比特币支付。

sentences.en: I didn't want a gift card.
sentences.zh: 我不想要礼品卡。

sentences.en: I didn't want some weird exchange.
sentences.zh: 我不想要什么奇怪的交易所。

sentences.en: I want to give you Bitcoin and you give me pizza.
sentences.zh: 我想给你比特币，你给我披萨。

sentences.en: People start developing new ways to spend Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 人们开始开发消费比特币的新方法。

sentences.en: People are sending it to each other instead of sending a Venmo payment or a PayPal payment.
sentences.zh: 人们开始互相转账，而不是发送 Venmo 付款或 PayPal 付款。

sentences.en: Some people are buying clothes with it.
sentences.zh: 有些人用它买衣服。

sentences.en: Some websites start accepting it as a form of payment.
sentences.zh: 一些网站开始接受它作为支付方式。

sentences.en: It becomes this viral phenomenon that people are very excited about.
sentences.zh: 它成为了一个病毒式的现象，人们对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Now it's starting to actually gain some traction.
sentences.zh: 现在它开始真正获得一些关注了。

sentences.en: And as it gets more attention and people get more excited about it, the price of Bitcoin keeps rising.
sentences.zh: 随着它获得更多关注，人们对它越来越兴奋，比特币的价格一直在上涨。

sentences.en: Bitcoins are booming.
sentences.zh: 比特币正在蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: Reaches, you know, $5,000 a Bitcoin and then $10,000 a Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 你知道，达到了每枚比特币5000美元，然后是1万美元。

sentences.en: And now it's up well past $50,000 a Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 现在已经远远超过每枚比特币5万美元了。

sentences.en: Cash is no longer king.
sentences.zh: 现金不再是王道。

sentences.en: And the reason why the price of Bitcoin keeps going up and up is because there are a finite number of Bitcoins.
sentences.zh: 比特币价格不断上涨的原因是因为比特币的数量是有限的。

sentences.en: So people are willing to pay more and more to acquire the limited number of them.
sentences.zh: 所以人们愿意支付越来越多的钱来获得数量有限的比特币。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so as that's happening, people are starting to create other different cryptocurrencies.
sentences.zh: 随着这种情况的发生，人们开始创造其他不同的加密货币。

sentences.en: Some of them are very serious, like Ethereum is a new one that pops up.
sentences.zh: 其中一些非常严肃，比如以太坊是一个涌现出来的新币种。

sentences.en: But there are also joke coins, or people call them shit coins sometimes.
sentences.zh: 但也有笑话币，或者人们有时称之为垃圾币。

sentences.en: There's a Dogecoin, which is like reference to this meme.
sentences.zh: 有一种狗狗币，就像是对这个网络迷因的引用。

sentences.en: There's a DentaCoin, cryptocurrency for dentists.
sentences.zh: 有一种牙医币，是牙医的加密货币。

sentences.en: There's Potcoin, which is the cryptocurrency for cannabis enthusiasts.
sentences.zh: 有一种大麻币，是大麻爱好者的加密货币。

sentences.en: There's even Bitcoen, which is the Jewish crypto token.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有犹太加密代币。

sentences.en: Oh boy.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So all of these start springing up.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些都开始涌现。

sentences.en: Most of them are worth absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 它们大多数毫无价值。

sentences.en: But then there's this quieter movement building of people who are using blockchains as a base technology to build lots of other things.
sentences.zh: 但随后出现了一种更安静的运动，人们开始使用区块链作为基础技术来构建许多其他东西。

sentences.en: Things like tracking the rights to photography online.
sentences.zh: 比如追踪网上摄影作品的版权。

sentences.en: So like if you're a photographer and you want to get credit and get paid when your photos are used,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是一名摄影师，当你的照片被使用时，你希望获得署名并获得报酬，

sentences.en: you could attach that information to a blockchain where it would be permanently and publicly available for people to see.
sentences.zh: 你可以将这些信息附加到区块链上，这样它就会永久且公开地供人们查看。

sentences.en: Like this photo belongs to Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 比如这张照片属于萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: This one belongs to Kevin.
sentences.zh: 这张属于凯文。

sentences.en: And when these photos get used, they get paid this much.
sentences.zh: 当这些照片被使用时，他们会得到这么多报酬。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: That seems huge, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上这似乎意义重大。

sentences.en: Yeah, it becomes a way to track the ownership and the ownership history of lots of different kinds of digital goods.
sentences.zh: 是的，它成为了一种追踪各种数字商品的所权以及所有权历史的方法。

sentences.en: And so one big moment for cryptocurrency comes when this other blockchain, Ethereum, allows you to create one-of-a-kind goods.
sentences.zh: 因此，加密货币的一个重大时刻是，另一个区块链以太坊允许你创造独一无二的商品。

sentences.en: Goods that can't be exchanged for other goods.
sentences.zh: 无法与其他商品交换的商品。

sentences.en: You know, if you have a Bitcoin, it doesn't really matter whether you have one Bitcoin or another Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你有一个比特币，你有一个比特币还是另一个比特币其实并不重要。

sentences.en: It's all Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 它们都是比特币。

sentences.en: But what Ethereum allows people to do is to say this is a one-of-a-kind asset and it can't be exchanged for any other asset.
sentences.zh: 但以太坊允许人们说，这是一个独一无二的资产，它不能与任何其他资产交换。

sentences.en: It is unique.
sentences.zh: 它是独一无二的。

sentences.en: So it's like a deed to a house or something?
sentences.zh: 所以就像房产契约之类的东西？

sentences.en: It's like a deed to a house or a certificate of authenticity that you might get if you buy a rare antique or something.
sentences.zh: 这就像房产契约，或者你买稀有古董时可能会获得的真品证书。

sentences.en: Ethereum allows you to kind of say this thing is mine and there's only one of them.
sentences.zh: 以太坊让你能够说这个东西是我的，而且世界上只有这一个。

sentences.en: And I can track its ownership forever.
sentences.zh: 我可以永远追踪它的所有权。

sentences.en: And anyone can go on the internet and see that I own this thing.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以在互联网上看到我拥有这个东西。

sentences.en: And this becomes known as the non-fungible token or NFT.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的不可替代代币或 NFT。

sentences.en: Non-fungible?
sentences.zh: 不可替代？

sentences.en: So fungible just means you can exchange one of it for any other one of it.
sentences.zh: 所以替代性意味着你可以用它的其中一个来交换它的任何其他一个。

sentences.en: So dollars are fungible because I can trade you a dollar and I have the same spending power with your dollar as I had with my dollar.
sentences.zh: 所以美元是具有替代性的，因为我可以跟你交换一美元，用你的美元和我用我的一美元拥有相同的购买力。

sentences.en: Something like an artwork is non-fungible because there's only one of them.
sentences.zh: 像艺术品这样的东西是不可替代的，因为世界上只有一件。

sentences.en: So if I have a renaissance painting, I'm not going to trade you for a poster of that painting because mine is the original.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我有一幅文艺复兴时期的画作，我是不会跟你换那幅画的海报的，因为我的是原作。

sentences.en: It's more valuable.
sentences.zh: 它更有价值。

sentences.en: And why would I give you my painting?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要给你我的画？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so basically people are discovering this ability to create just one of something on the internet.
sentences.zh: 基本上，人们现在发现了一种能在互联网上创造独一无二物品的能力。

sentences.en: Before this, things that were on the internet were just infinitely copyable.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，互联网上的东西都是可以无限复制的。

sentences.en: If you had a song or a photo, you could copy and paste that any number of times.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一首歌或一张照片，你可以任意次数地复制粘贴它。

sentences.en: And every copy would be exactly the same and totally indistinguishable from every other copy.
sentences.zh: 而且每一个复制品都完全相同，与其他任何复制品没有任何区别。

sentences.en: But what the Ethereum blockchain allows people to do is to stamp these digital objects with sort of a certificate of authenticity.
sentences.zh: 但以太坊区块链允许人们做的是，给这些数字对象打上某种真实性证书。

sentences.en: To say, this is the original of this item and you can't copy or fake the digital signature that is sort of attached to that item.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这是该物品的原件，你无法复制或伪造附着在该物品上的数字签名。

sentences.en: Can I ask a really stupid question at this point?
sentences.zh: 我这时候能问一个特别蠢的问题吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: Is the NFT the thing or is the NFT the digital stamp of authenticity of the thing?
sentences.zh: NFT 是那个东西本身，还是那个东西的数字防伪戳？

sentences.en: Great question.
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: It is a token that represents a thing.
sentences.zh: 它是一个代表某个事物的代币。

sentences.en: When you have an NFT of an image or a video clip, the NFT is not the image or the video clip itself.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有某个图像或视频剪辑的 NFT 时，NFT 并不是图像或视频剪辑本身。

sentences.en: It's the certificate of authenticity that attaches to that thing and links to it.
sentences.zh: 它是附加在该事物上并与之链接的真实性证书。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I think I understand.
sentences.zh: 我想我懂了。

sentences.en: With NFTs, you can still make a copy, but this allows us to know which one is the original, which one exactly.
sentences.zh: 有了 NFT，你仍然可以进行复制，但这让我们知道哪一个是原件，究竟哪一个是原件。

sentences.en: And we can assign value to that original and see the whole story of buying and selling that original item.
sentences.zh: 我们可以为那个原件赋予价值，并查看买卖该原件的整个过程。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: It's a way to keep track of ownership and where something came from.
sentences.zh: 这是一种追踪所有权和物品来源的方法。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, Kevin, there are these things, non-fungible tokens or NFTs.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯文，有这样一种东西，叫非同质化代币或 NFT。

sentences.en: What do people do with them?
sentences.zh: 人们用它来做什么？

sentences.en: So, for a while, people are just sort of thinking about the theoretical possibility of NFTs.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，人们只是在思考 NFT 的理论可能性。

sentences.en: And then in about 2017, people actually start creating them.
sentences.zh: 然后在 2017 年左右，人们实际上开始创造它们了。

sentences.en: So, the first NFTs are kind of these crypto art projects.
sentences.zh: 所以，最早的 NFT 有点像这种加密艺术项目。

sentences.en: There's this thing called CryptoPunks, which is this set of cartoon characters that people started treating as digital action figures.
sentences.zh: 有个叫 CryptoPunks 的东西，它是一套卡通形象，人们开始把它们当成数字版办家家酒的人偶。

sentences.en: And other people would take memes, like popular graphics, and turn them into NFTs and sell the NFT.
sentences.zh: 其他人则会把表情包等流行的图形变成 NFT，并出售 NFT。

sentences.en: This thing that represented, like, this is the one true version of this meme.
sentences.zh: 这种代表“这就是这个表情包唯一真正版本”的东西。

sentences.en: And then, last year, they really exploded.
sentences.zh: 然后，就在去年，它们真的爆发了。

sentences.en: You've got songs, music, videos, memes, even tweets of Lindsay Lohan's face, all becoming NFTs.
sentences.zh: 你看到歌曲、音乐、视频、表情包，甚至林赛·罗韩脸部的推文，都变成了 NFT。

sentences.en: People started buying NFTs of sports videos.
sentences.zh: 人们开始购买体育视频的 NFT。

sentences.en: Our next guest is the first NFL player to get involved in the NFT craze, launching a new line of exclusive digital trading cards this morning.
sentences.zh: 我们的下一位嘉宾是第一位参与 NFT 热潮的 NFL 球员，他今天早上推出了全新系列的独家数字交易卡。

sentences.en: And I am proud to be launching the Rob Gronkowski Championship Series NFT collection.
sentences.zh: 我很荣幸能推出罗布·格隆考斯基冠军系列 NFT 收藏品。

sentences.en: Star Tom Brady announced he's launching an NFT company called Autograph.
sentences.zh: 明星汤姆·布雷迪宣布他将成立一家名为 Autograph 的 NFT 公司。

sentences.en: A clip of LeBron James dunking became an NFT and was sold for more than $200,000.
sentences.zh: 勒布朗·詹姆斯扣篮的一段视频剪辑变成了 NFT，并以超过 20 万美元的价格售出。

sentences.en: Jack Dorsey, the CEO of Twitter, sold his first ever tweet as an NFT for $2.9 million.
sentences.zh: 推特首席执行官杰克·多西以 290 万美元的价格卖出了他的第一条推文的 NFT。

sentences.en: I don't know about you, but this sounds nuts.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你怎么想，但这听起来太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Where do you hang the NFT in the living room?
sentences.zh: 你要把 NFT 挂在客厅的哪里？

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, over the mantel?
sentences.zh: 比如，挂在壁炉架上方？

sentences.en: And earlier this year, the biggest NFT sale ever happened.
sentences.zh: 就在今年早些时候，史上最大的一笔 NFT 交易诞生了。

sentences.en: Christie's, the auction house, auctioned off a collection of digital art by this digital artist named Beeple for $69 million.
sentences.zh: 佳士得拍卖行以 6900 万美元的价格拍出了一位名叫比普尔的数字艺术家创作的一系列数字艺术品。

sentences.en: And that was sort of...
sentences.zh: 这简直有点……

sentences.en: $69 million?
Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's more than most Picassos, Monets, or Warhols.
sentences.zh: 这比大多数毕加索、莫奈或沃霍尔的作品还要贵。

sentences.en: Beauty's in the eye of the NFT beholder here, Carl.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，美在于 NFT 购买者的眼中。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, it's like, wow, this is a real market.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，感觉就像，哇，这是一个真正的市场。

sentences.en: People are really willing to pay for these tokens, these digital certificates of authenticity.
sentences.zh: 人们真的愿意为这些代币、这些数字真实性证书付费。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of money to be made here.
sentences.zh: 这里面有巨大的商机。

sentences.en: So I thought to myself, why should LeBron James and Jack Dorsey have all the fun?
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，凭什么勒布朗·詹姆斯和杰克·多西能占尽所有乐子？

sentences.en: Why can't I make and sell my own NFT?
sentences.zh: 为什么我不能制作并出售我自己的 NFT？

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App 时，你在 App 内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall, to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能看到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》App，即可获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Kevin, you see this world of NFTs kind of going crazy, gaining traction.
sentences.zh: 所以，凯文，你看到这个 NFT 世界正变得疯狂，势头强劲。

sentences.en: And you, Kevin Roos, a New York Times journalist, decide to sell an NFT yourself.
sentences.zh: 而你，凯文·罗斯，《纽约时报》的一名记者，决定自己卖一个 NFT。

sentences.en: So what do you do?
sentences.zh: 那么你是怎么做的？

sentences.en: What's the first thing you do?
sentences.zh: 你做的第一件事是什么？

sentences.en: So I decided that I would write a column explaining NFTs.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定写一篇专栏文章来解释 NFT。

sentences.en: And then I would turn that column into an NFT and sell it.
sentences.zh: 然后我要把那篇专栏文章变成一个 NFT 并把它卖掉。

sentences.en: And whatever we made would go to the Neediest Cases Fund, which is the New York Times' charity.
sentences.zh: 我们赚到的任何钱都将捐给“最需要帮助者基金”，这是《纽约时报》的慈善机构。

sentences.en: So I wrote the column.
sentences.zh: 所以我写了这篇专栏。

sentences.en: And then I had a graphic created of the column.
sentences.zh: 然后我让人把这篇专栏制作成了一张图表。

sentences.en: And I took that graphic, the picture of my column, and I then did what's called minting an NFT.
sentences.zh: 我拿着那个图表，也就是我专栏的照片，然后进行了所谓的铸造 NFT。

sentences.en: I actually created the NFT and put it on the blockchain.
sentences.zh: 我实际上创建了 NFT 并将其放到了区块链上。

sentences.en: And then it was ready to be sold.
sentences.zh: 然后它就可以出售了。

sentences.en: And what happens once you get the NFT on the blockchain?
sentences.zh: 把 NFT 放到区块链上之后会发生什么？

sentences.en: I mean, is there like, I don't know, confetti or balloons or something that appear on your screen?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，屏幕上会出现什么，比方说，彩带、气球之类的东西吗？

sentences.en: Like, what does it look like?
sentences.zh: 看起来是什么样的？

sentences.en: Yeah, Jack Dorsey shows up at your house and gives you a bag full of cash.
sentences.zh: 对，杰克·多西会来到你家，给你塞满一包现金。

sentences.en: No, it basically just says this thing lives on the blockchain now.
sentences.zh: 不，它基本上只是说这个东西现在存在于区块链上了。

sentences.en: It is here.
sentences.zh: 它就在这里。

sentences.en: And once you have the NFT, then you have to actually set up the auction to sell it.
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了 NFT，你实际上就必须建立拍卖来出售它。

sentences.en: So the auction is not run by humans.
sentences.zh: 所以拍卖不是由人类运营的。

sentences.en: They're run by software.
sentences.zh: 它们是由软件运行的。

sentences.en: You have some choices to make.
sentences.zh: 你有一些选择要做。

sentences.en: So one thing you can do when you're selling an NFT is to set a royalty.
sentences.zh: 当你出售 NFT 时，你可以做的一件事就是设置版税。

sentences.en: Essentially saying that, you know, if someone buys it for $100 and then resells it for $200 to someone else, the artist, the person who originally uploaded that,
sentences.zh: 本质上就是说，你知道，如果有人以 100 美元买下它，然后以 200 美元的价格转售给其他人，那么艺术家，也就是最初上传该物品的人，

sentences.en: can get a portion of that sale forever.
sentences.zh: 可以永远获得该销售额的一部分。

sentences.en: And that's sort of built into the code of the auction.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是内置在拍卖代码中的。

sentences.en: So that would essentially allow you to continue to make money each time the thing is sold, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上能让你在每次该物品售出时继续赚钱，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's part of what makes NFTs really attractive to artists because, you know, if you're selling physical paintings, you sell it to someone,
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么 NFT 对艺术家非常有吸引力的一部分原因，因为你知道，如果你出售实体画作，你把它卖给某人，

sentences.en: they resell it to someone else for a lot more money, and you don't get a cut of that as the artiSt.
sentences.zh: 他们以更高的价格把它转售给其他人，而作为艺术家的你分不到一杯羹。

sentences.en: But with NFTs, you can build it into the code that every time it's resold forever, the artist, the original person who uploaded the file can get paid a fraction of that.
sentences.zh: 但在 NFT 中，你可以把代码内置其中，这样无论何时它被永远转售，艺术家、最初上传文件的原作者都可以获得其中的一小部分报酬。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a really big difference.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大的区别。

sentences.en: You can also set a minimum acceptable price.
sentences.zh: 你还可以设定一个最低接受价格。

sentences.en: So like, what is the lowest amount of money I would be willing to sell my NFT for?
sentences.zh: 比如，我愿意出售我的 NFT 的最低金额是多少？

sentences.en: And I was feeling pretty optimistic.
sentences.zh: 我当时感觉非常乐观。

sentences.en: I thought maybe, maybe someone out there, some New York Times reader will have some Ethereum, you know, burning a hole in their digital wallet,
sentences.zh: 我想也许，也许会有那么一个人，某个《纽约时报》的读者，他的数字钱包里有些以太坊，烧得慌，

sentences.en: and they'll decide my column is worth half an Ether, about $850.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会觉得我的专栏值半个以太币，大约 850 美元。

sentences.en: So I set the minimum price, and I listed the auction and simultaneously published my story about the auction.
sentences.zh: 所以我设定了最低价格，发布了拍卖，并同时发表了我关于这次拍卖的故事。

sentences.en: And so then it was just on the blockchain, up for sale.
sentences.zh: 然后它就呆在区块链上待售了。

sentences.en: Okay, so what happens?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那接下来呢？

sentences.en: So immediately I start, my colleagues start joking about the fact that no one's going to bid on my dumb NFT.
sentences.zh: 所以我刚开始时，我的同事们开始开玩笑说根本没有人会出价买我这个愚蠢的 NFT。

sentences.en: There's a Slack thread with some of my colleagues where they're sort of betting on how much it's going to sell for.
sentences.zh: 我和一些同事在 Slack 线程里，他们甚至在打赌这玩意儿能卖多少钱。

sentences.en: The consensus is that it's not going to go for much.
sentences.zh: 大家的共识是它卖不了多少钱。

sentences.en: So I listed in the morning, and at first, there are just a couple bids.
sentences.zh: 所以我早上挂牌，起初只有几个出价。

sentences.en: And, you know, someone bids the minimum $850, and then there's $1,000 and $1,200.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有人出价最低的 850 美元，然后是 1000 美元和 1200 美元。

sentences.en: And I'm going, okay, we're going to make some money here.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，好吧，我们这下能赚点钱了。

sentences.en: And before I went to bed that night, I checked again, and the top bid had risen to more than $30,000, which was like mind-blowing to me.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上睡觉前，我又看了一眼，最高出价已经涨到了 3 万多美元，这对我来说简直太震撼了。

sentences.en: I was like, this picture, this NFT, is now worth more than basically anything else I own.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，这张图片、这个 NFT，现在比我拥有的几乎任何东西都值钱。

sentences.en: Crazy.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking, this is insane.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这太离谱了。

sentences.en: This is going to make a great story.
sentences.zh: 这会是一个很好的故事素材。

sentences.en: Can you believe it?
sentences.zh: 你敢相信吗？

sentences.en: $30,000 for a picture of my column.
sentences.zh: 我专栏的一张图片竟然卖了 3 万美元。

sentences.en: Then I wake up the next morning, and the chaos starts.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天早上醒来，混乱就开始了。

sentences.en: So, the auction is supposed to last for 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 所以，拍卖本应持续 24 小时。

sentences.en: And in the last, I would say, hour of that, a bidding war breaks out.
sentences.zh: 我想说，在最后的那个小时里，一场竞标战爆发了。

sentences.en: It started going up and up and up.
sentences.zh: 它开始不断往上涨。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And I was just watching my computer screen and refreshing and just agog.
sentences.zh: 我当时只是盯着电脑屏幕，不断刷新，惊得目瞪口呆。

sentences.en: Like, I couldn't, I was like, is this real?
sentences.zh: 就像，我简直不敢相信，我在想，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Like, am I being pranked here?
sentences.zh: 就像，我是不是被恶作剧了？

sentences.en: So, in the final minutes of this auction, it went from 100 Ether, which was about $160,000,
sentences.zh: 所以，在这个拍卖的最后几分钟，它从 100 个以太币（约合 16 万美元），

sentences.en: all the way up to the final sale price, which was 350 Ether, which, at the time, was about $560,000, but is now about $725,000.
sentences.zh: 一路飙升到最终成交价 350 个以太币，当时约合 56 万美元，而现在大约是 72.5 万美元。

sentences.en: Kevin, it is crazy.
sentences.zh: 凯文，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I mean, no offense, but, like, your column, in my mind, it is not worth the price of a nice house.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，无意冒犯，但像你的专栏，在我看来，它不值一栋好房子的价格。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a good column, but, you know, house, column, house, column.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一篇好专栏，但是，你知道，房子，专栏，房子，专栏。

sentences.en: No, I mean, I, you know, generally have decent self-esteem, and even I was like, there's nothing
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，我，你知道的，通常有不错的自尊心，即便如此我也觉得没有任何东西

sentences.en: I've ever written is worth this much money.
sentences.zh: 我写过的内容能值这么多钱。

sentences.en: But also, Kevin, especially when I can read it for free online.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，凯文，特别是当我可以在网上免费阅读它的时候。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that was the thing that was so crazy, is, like, you could go on NYTimes.com and read this entire thing for free.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最疯狂的就是这一点，你可以登录 NYTimes.com 免费阅读完整内容。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I just stared at my monitor, just laughing uncontrollably, just, like, totally in shock about what had happened.
sentences.zh: 我只是盯着显示器，情不自禁地大笑，简直被发生的事情惊呆了。

sentences.en: So, Kevin, who bought this?
sentences.zh: 所以，凯文，是谁买的？

sentences.en: And more importantly, why did someone buy your column for the price of a nice house?
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，为什么有人会用一套好房子的价格来买你的专栏？

sentences.en: A really nice house.
sentences.zh: 一套非常不错的房子。

sentences.en: I'd like to think they just have good taste.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿认为他们只是品味好。

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 拜托。

sentences.en: More realistically, the winner of the auction, I don't know for sure who it is, but their username was 3F Music, and they appear to be a music production company based in Dubai.
sentences.zh: 更现实一点说，拍卖的赢家，我不知道具体是谁，但他们的用户名是 3F Music，他们似乎是一家总部位于迪拜的音乐制作公司。

sentences.en: And they are a prominent NFT collector.
sentences.zh: 他们是著名的 NFT 收藏家。

sentences.en: And so I did reach out to 3F Music.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实联系了 3F Music。

sentences.en: I also reached out to a number of other people who bid on the auction.
sentences.zh: 我还联系了其他许多参与竞标的人。

sentences.en: And I asked them why.
sentences.zh: 我问他们为什么。

sentences.en: And for some of them, especially the early bidders who were bidding relatively small amounts
sentences.zh: 对其中一些人来说，尤其是那些出价相对较少的早期竞标者，

sentences.en: of money, they thought of this as just a fun transaction that might get them some publicity.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这只是一笔有趣的交易，可能会为他们带来一些知名度。

sentences.en: So I should say, in addition to the NFT of this column, I also said that I would write a follow-up column about the auction and feature the winner.
sentences.zh: 所以我应该说，除了这个专栏的 NFT 之外，我还说过我会写一篇关于这次拍卖的后续专栏，并将赢家写进去。

sentences.en: And so I think for some of them, it was like, this is a price I'm willing to pay to get into the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对他们中的一些人来说，这就好像是，这是我愿意付出以进入《纽约时报》的代价。

sentences.en: But then at a certain point, I would say around $10,000 or so, I started to hear other explanations.
sentences.zh: 但到了某个阶段，大概在 1 万美元左右，我开始听到其他的解释。

sentences.en: And some of them were basically saying this was a speculative investment.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人基本上把这说成是一种投机投资。

sentences.en: So they were bidding on this NFT because it was the first NFT created by the New York
sentences.zh: 所以他们竞标这个 NFT，是因为这是《纽约时报》

sentences.en: Times.
sentences.zh: 创作的第一个 NFT。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's sort of like a status attached to the first of something.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，成为某事物的第一个往往带有某种地位的象征。

sentences.en: And so they thought NFTs become a huge industry.
sentences.zh: 因此他们认为 NFT 会成为一个巨大的行业。

sentences.en: Then owning the first one from the New York Times, I might be able to resell that for more money later on.
sentences.zh: 那么拥有《纽约时报》发行的第一个，我以后可能可以高价转手。

sentences.en: I also talked to some people who said that this was essentially like an ideological statement for them.
sentences.zh: 我也和一些人聊过，他们说这本质上对他们来说是一种意识形态的表态。

sentences.en: I talked to one musician who actually bid on my NFT who said that, you know, he had grown
sentences.zh: 我采访了一位实际对我的 NFT 出价的音乐家，他说，你知道，他是在

sentences.en: up in the era of Napster when songs were first able to be copied and distributed on the internet for free.
sentences.zh: Napster 时代长大的，当时歌曲首次能够被复制并在互联网上免费分发。

sentences.en: And piracy became a huge problem.
sentences.zh: 盗版成为了一个大问题。

sentences.en: And that blockchain technology and NFTs had changed that by basically allowing digital goods to have scarcity, which is what gives physical goods their value.
sentences.zh: 而区块链技术和 NFT 改变了这一点，它基本上让数字商品具备了稀缺性，而这正是赋予实物价值的东西。

sentences.en: So this musician said basically that collecting NFTs was less about owning the actual NFT, but more about sort of signaling optimism and belief in this new ownership model.
sentences.zh: 所以这位音乐家基本上说，收集 NFT 与其说是为了拥有实际的 NFT，不如说是为了表达对这种新所有权模式的乐观和信仰。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you have the speculators, you have people who are trying to invest, but you also have people who care about art and intellectual property who are trying to make a statement,
sentences.zh: 所以你既有投机者，有试图投资的人，但也有关心艺术和知识产权、试图表明立场的人，

sentences.en: which I think is pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, $500,000 is just so much money.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我的意思是，50 万美元真的是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: So was there some deeper reason for this purchase, do you think?
sentences.zh: 所以你认为这次购买背后有什么更深层的原因吗？

sentences.en: I mean, not only your column, but these other crazy high prices for sort of seemingly cheap things.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不仅是你的专栏，还有这些针对看似廉价的东西的高得离谱的价格。

sentences.en: It's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of possible answers.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多可能的答案。

sentences.en: You know, wealth inequality is obviously part of the equation, the fact that there are people with this much disposable income.
sentences.zh: 你知道，财富不平等显然是其中的一部分，事实是确实有人拥有这么多可支配收入。

sentences.en: And one of the artists I talked to who bid on the auction actually said, you know, this isn't actually that strange in the offline world.
sentences.zh: 我采访的参与竞拍的艺术家之一实际上说过，你知道，这在现实世界中其实并不那么奇怪。

sentences.en: Rich people spend vast sums of money on things of dubious value all the time.
sentences.zh: 富人们总是把巨额资金花在价值可疑的东西上。

sentences.en: They fly off to art fairs.
sentences.zh: 他们飞去参加艺术博览会。

sentences.en: They spend millions of dollars on sculptures and pieces of art for their walls.
sentences.zh: 他们花数百万美元购买雕塑和艺术品挂在墙上。

sentences.en: Or maybe they don't even have the art on their walls.
sentences.zh: 或者也许他们的墙上根本没有挂艺术品。

sentences.en: Maybe it's just they're trading pieces of art that live in a warehouse somewhere.
sentences.zh: 也许他们只是在交易存放在某个仓库里的艺术品。

sentences.en: And so all they really have is the knowledge that they own a thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们真正拥有的只是他们拥有这样东西的认知。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's like a new Birkin bag or owning a Warhol.
sentences.zh: 就像一个新的铂金包或者拥有一个沃霍尔的作品。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think that for some people who are investing tons of money in NFTs, we can't underestimate the role that just emotion and status and bragging rights play in all this.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，对于一些在 NFT 上投入巨资的人来说，我们不能低估单纯的情感、地位和炫耀资本在其中所起的作用。

sentences.en: Okay, that kind of brings us all the way back to the very beginning, Kevin, because the point
sentences.zh: 好的，凯文，这把我们完全带回了最初的话题，因为你刚刚

sentences.en: you just made about NFTs and how they operate, it's kind of similar to how we've always valued things.
sentences.zh: 提出的关于 NFT 及其运作方式的观点，其实和我们一直以来评估事物价值的方式有点相似。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering, you know, if you go back to the conversation about the blockchain, we were
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，你知道，如果回到关于区块链的对话，我们

sentences.en: thinking about what Nakamoto was trying to solve for, you know, he wanted to fundamentally change the financial system and how it works.
sentences.zh: 在思考中本聪试图解决什么问题，你知道，他想要从根本上改变金融系统及其运作方式。

sentences.en: But did he succeed?
sentences.zh: 但他成功了吗？

sentences.en: Or has he just created some different system in which we operate basically in the same way, with the same kind of human emotion motivations?
sentences.zh: 还是说他只是创造了另一个系统，而我们在其中以完全相同的方式运作，带着同样的人类情感动机？

sentences.en: Did he just create a thing to covet?
sentences.zh: 他只是创造了一个让人垂涎的东西吗？

sentences.en: Or did he actually do something truly new?
sentences.zh: 还是说他真的做出了一些真正崭新的东西？

sentences.en: So I think there are sort of two ways to look at something like NFTs.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为看待像 NFT 这样的事物大致有两种方式。

sentences.en: On one level, I think, yes, as you said, like, it's just taking something that existed offline,
sentences.zh: 从某种层面上讲，我认为，正如你所说，是的，它只是拿走了现实世界中存在的事物，

sentences.en: this concept of scarcity, of having one of something and having that quality of scarcity be the thing that gives an object its value.
sentences.zh: 即稀缺性的概念，拥有某物的一个副本，并让这种稀缺性品质成为赋予物体价值的东西。

sentences.en: And you're translating that onto the internet, where it really hadn't existed before.
sentences.zh: 而你正在把它带到互联网上，而它以前在那里并不真正存在。

sentences.en: So even if NFTs are just a way of kind of replicating the scarcity that objects can have in the offline world, that's an incredibly valuable thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使 NFT 只是复制现实世界中物体可能具备的稀缺性的一种方式，这也是一件极其有价值的事情。

sentences.en: But I think there's this other change happening, this generational transformation that's happening as more of our lives move onto the internet.
sentences.zh: 但我认为还有另一种变革正在发生，随着我们越来越多的生活转移到互联网上，这种代际转变正在发生。

sentences.en: I mean, we spend so much time in the offline world, sort of curating our surroundings, you know, putting art on our walls, figuring out what car to drive, what house to buy,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在现实世界中花了大量时间，来策划我们的周围环境，你知道，在墙上挂艺术品，弄清楚开什么车，买什么房子，

sentences.en: what neighborhood to live in, like expressing ourselves through the consumption of scarce goods and building identities around the physical objects that we own.
sentences.zh: 住在哪个社区，就像是通过消费稀缺商品来表达自我，并围绕我们拥有的实体物品构建身份认同一样。

sentences.en: And now with NFTs, that aspect of life, kind of figuring out what to buy to signal who we are and what we value, that can also be online.
sentences.zh: 现在有了 NFT，生活的那个方面——弄清楚买什么来表明我们是谁以及我们珍视什么——也可以在线上进行了。

sentences.en: Maybe the thing that gives you status and identity is not a physical object.
sentences.zh: 也许赋予你地位和身份认同的不是实体物品。

sentences.en: Maybe it's a token on the blockchain.
sentences.zh: 也许它是区块链上的一个代币。

sentences.en: Thanks so much, Kevin.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，凯文。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: This appears to me, from what I've viewed, and the officer's reaction in distress immediately
sentences.zh: 在我看来，从我所看到的以及警员随后的痛苦反应来看，

sentences.en: after, that this was an accidental discharge that resulted in the tragic death of Mr. Wright.
sentences.zh: 这是一次意外走火，导致了赖特先生的悲惨死亡。

sentences.en: As outcry and protests grew over the shooting of Daunte Wright, an unarmed Black man killed
sentences.zh: 随着针对枪杀小唐特·赖特的抗议和声讨愈演愈烈，小唐特·赖特是一名无辜的黑人男子，在明尼阿波利斯郊区与警员遭遇时被杀害，

sentences.en: during an encounter with police officers in a suburb of Minneapolis, local officials said that the officer who shot Wright appeared to have done so by accident.
sentences.zh: 当地官员表示，开枪打死赖特的警员似乎是出于意外。

sentences.en: After stopping Wright for a traffic violation, police in the city of Brooklyn Center discovered there was a warrant for his arreSt.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克林森市警方在因交通违章拦下赖特后，发现他有一张逮捕令。

sentences.en: According to police, Wright stepped back into his car, triggering a struggle with officers.
sentences.zh: 据警方称，赖特退回到他的车里，引发了与警员的争执。

sentences.en: Video of that encounter, recorded by the officer's body camera, shows that she repeatedly yelled
sentences.zh: 警员随身摄像头记录下的这段遭遇的视频显示，她在开枪前多次大喊

sentences.en: taser before discharging her gun and immediately expressed surprise after shooting Wright.
sentences.zh: 泰瑟枪，并在枪击赖特后立即表现出惊讶。

sentences.en: As I watched the video and listened to the officer's commands, it is my belief that the officer
sentences.zh: 当我观看视频并聆听警员的指令时，我认为这位警员

sentences.en: had the intention to deploy their taser, but instead shot Mr. Wright with a single bullet.
sentences.zh: 本意是使用泰瑟枪，但却用一颗子弹击中了赖特先生。

sentences.en: The shooting occurred less than 10 miles from the courtroom, where former Minneapolis
sentences.zh: 枪击事件发生地距离法庭不到 10 英里，前明尼阿波利斯

sentences.en: police officer Derek Chauvin is on trial for the murder of George Floyd, and on Monday, the Biden administration urged
sentences.zh: 警员德里克·肖万正因谋杀乔治·弗洛伊德在那里受审，周一，拜登政府敦促

sentences.en: the governor of Michigan, Gretchen Whitmer, to lock down her state to slow what has become the nation's worst outbreak of COVID-19 infections.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州州长格雷琴·惠特默封锁她的州，以遏制已成为全美最严重的 COVID-19 感染疫情。

sentences.en: But Whitmer remains resistant and instead called for a surge in vaccinations in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 但惠特默依然抗拒，转而呼吁在密歇根州激增疫苗接种。

sentences.en: When you have an acute situation, an extraordinary number of cases like we have in Michigan, the answer is not necessarily to give vaccine.
sentences.zh: 当你遇到严峻局势，像我们在密歇根州那样拥有数量惊人的病例时，解决方案不一定就是发放疫苗。

sentences.en: In fact, we know that…
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们知道……

sentences.en: That suggestion was rejected by the head of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention,
sentences.zh: 这一建议遭到疾病控制与预防中心负责人

sentences.en: Rochelle Walensky.
sentences.zh: 罗谢尔·瓦伦斯基的拒绝。

sentences.en: The answer to that is to really close things down, to go back to our basics, to go back to where we were
sentences.zh: 对此的解决方案确实是实施封锁，回到我们的基础，回到我们去年春天、去年夏天的状态，

sentences.en: last spring, last summer, and to shut things down, to flatten the curve, to decrease contact with one another, to test to the extent that we have available…
sentences.zh: 实施封锁，拉平曲线，减少彼此接触，并在我们力所能及的范围内进行检测……

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由斯特拉·谭、罗谢尔·邦贾和妮娜·庞蒂克制作。

sentences.zh: 由佩奇·考维特和雷切尔·奎斯特剪辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.zh: 这就是《今日早报》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 收听节目，了解如何让你的客宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.zh: 他们是深度睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean, do they black out to go to sleep?
sentences.zh: 我不是指，他们会不会晕过去才能睡着？

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
